title: The clear light at death
hookLine: at death, the teachings say, a clear light dawns
carry: the clear light is your own mind

lines: WHEN THE OTHER LIGHTS GO OUT.
cards: A summer night, and the whole city loses power at once. Streetlights, windows, billboards, gone. People stand on their porches, a little uneasy.
Then someone looks up and says, oh. Above the rooftops the sky is full of stars, more than anyone on the block has seen there in years. They hadn't arrived.
They'd been there the whole time, drowned out by all the other lights.
Tibetan teachers say something like that happens at the end of a life: when every other light goes out, something that was always shining shows itself. Today: the clear light.

teach.h: ÖSEL: THE MIND'S OWN NATURE, BARE.
teach.b: First, what the teachings say. At the end of the bardo of dying, when the senses have withdrawn and the breath has stopped, a clear light dawns.
Tibetans call it ösel, and teachers describe it like a clear sky, empty of clouds. It isn't a light from outside, they say. It's the mind's own nature, bare.
The Bardo Thödol speaks to the person at that moment, by name: this is your own mind. Recognize it. Second, the mother and the child.
Glimpses of the mind's nature met in meditation during life are called the child clear light. The clear light at death is called the mother.
If the child has been met often enough, they say, the two recognize each other and meet like a child running into its mother's lap. That's why a lifetime of practice matters for this moment.
Third, an older echo, the luminous mind you met in year two.

teach.h: A LUMINOUS MIND, STAINED BY VISITORS.
teach.b: In a short Pali discourse, the Buddha says the mind is luminous, stained by defilements that arrive like visitors. Some readers hear the same intuition there: underneath the passing stains, something clear.
The two speak in their own ways, and neither needs the other to make its point. Fourth, why this is taught to the living.
Teachers say small glimpses come every day: in the gap after a thought, at the edge of sleep, in the moment after a sneeze or a surprise, before the mind starts talking again.
The practice, in this teaching, is learning to notice the stars before the lights go out.

how: Tibetan Buddhists prepare for death by practicing recognition of the mind's nature in meditation, the 'child' clear light, so that the 'mother' clear light at death may be recognized; the Bardo Thödol is read aloud to remind the one who has died.

o: the mind's own bare nature, dawning at death
a lamp kept burning beside a person who has died
a bright tunnel the dead walk toward to find peace

games.q: the clear light: tap the pairs.
p: the light that dawns at death

s: the clear light is a light coming from outside the person
the teachers say it is the mind's own nature, bare, with nothing covering it.
Tibetan teachers say glimpses can come in daily life
in the gap after a thought, at the edge of sleep, after a surprise.
in the Pali discourse, the stains on the mind arrive like visitors
the Buddha says the mind is luminous and stained by defilements that arrive.

games.q: at death, the clear light dawns. what does the text read beside the one who has died tell them?
o: this is your own mind. recognize it.
this is a light from somewhere else. follow it.
close your eyes until it passes.
games.why: the Bardo Thödol speaks to the person by name: the clear light is the mind's own nature, to be recognized.

practice: Close your eyes for three easy breaths, then open them slowly and catch the moment the room appears, before you name a single thing in it. Let the seeing be wide and plain, like the stars that were there all along.
If thinking about death weighs on you today, you don't have to carry it alone: call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: The clear light. In Tibetan teaching, the mind's own nature, bare and luminous, which dawns at death and can be glimpsed in life. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit prabhasvara, luminous; Pali pabhassara, the word for the luminous mind.

carryVoice: Your line: the clear light is your own mind. The stars were there all along. Same time tomorrow.
